scene.label: Act 3, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. Another part of the heath

content.text: Storm continues. Enter Lear and Fool.

lines.text: Blow, winds, and crack your cheeks! Rage! blow!
lines.plainText: Blow winds and crack your cheeks Rage blow

lines.text: You cataracts and hurricanoes, spout
lines.plainText: You cataracts and hurricanoes spout

lines.text: Till you have drench'd our steeples, drown'd the cocks!
lines.plainText: Till you have drench'd our steeples drown'd the cocks

lines.text: You sulphurous and thought-executing fires,
lines.plainText: You sulphurous and thoughtexecuting fires

lines.text: Vaunt-couriers to oak-cleaving thunderbolts,
lines.plainText: Vauntcouriers to oakcleaving thunderbolts

lines.text: Singe my white head! And thou, all-shaking thunder,
lines.plainText: Singe my white head And thou allshaking thunder

lines.text: Strike flat the thick rotundity o' the world!
lines.plainText: Strike flat the thick rotundity o' the world

lines.text: Crack nature's moulds, all germens spill at once,
lines.plainText: Crack nature's moulds all germens spill at once

lines.text: That make ingrateful man!
lines.plainText: That make ingrateful man

lines.text: O nuncle, court holy-water in a dry house is better than this rain-water out o' door. Good nuncle, in; and ask thy daughters blessing: here's a night pities neither wise men nor fools.
lines.plainText: O nuncle court holywater in a dry house is better than this rainwater out o' door Good nuncle in and ask thy daughters blessing here's a night pities neither wise men nor fools

lines.text: Rumble thy bellyful! Spit, fire! spout, rain!
lines.plainText: Rumble thy bellyful Spit fire spout rain

lines.text: Nor rain, wind, thunder, fire are my daughters;
lines.plainText: Nor rain wind thunder fire are my daughters

lines.text: I tax not you, you elements, with unkindness.
lines.plainText: I tax not you you elements with unkindness

lines.text: I never gave you kingdom, call'd you children;
lines.plainText: I never gave you kingdom call'd you children

lines.text: You owe me no subscription: then let fall
lines.plainText: You owe me no subscription then let fall

lines.text: Your horrible pleasure. Here I stand your slave,
lines.plainText: Your horrible pleasure Here I stand your slave

lines.text: A poor, infirm, weak, and despis'd old man:
lines.plainText: A poor infirm weak and despis'd old man

lines.text: But yet I call you servile ministers,
lines.plainText: But yet I call you servile ministers

lines.text: That will with two pernicious daughters join
lines.plainText: That will with two pernicious daughters join

lines.text: Your high-engender'd battles 'gainst a head
lines.plainText: Your highengender'd battles 'gainst a head

lines.text: So old and white as this! O! O! 'tis foul!
lines.plainText: So old and white as this O O 'tis foul

lines.text: He that has a house to put's head in has a good head-piece.
lines.plainText: He that has a house to put's head in has a good headpiece

lines.text: The codpiece that will house
lines.plainText: The codpiece that will house

lines.text: Before the head has any,
lines.plainText: Before the head has any

lines.text: The head and he shall louse:
lines.plainText: The head and he shall louse

lines.text: So beggars marry many.
lines.plainText: So beggars marry many

lines.text: The man that makes his toe
lines.plainText: The man that makes his toe

lines.text: What he his heart should make
lines.plainText: What he his heart should make

lines.text: Shall of a corn cry woe,
lines.plainText: Shall of a corn cry woe

lines.text: And turn his sleep to wake.
lines.plainText: And turn his sleep to wake

lines.text: For there was never yet fair woman but she made mouths in a glass.
lines.plainText: For there was never yet fair woman but she made mouths in a glass

lines.text: No, I will be the pattern of all patience;
lines.plainText: No I will be the pattern of all patience

lines.text: I will say nothing.
lines.plainText: I will say nothing

lines.text: Who's there?
lines.plainText: Who's there

lines.text: Marry, here's grace and a codpiece; that's a wise man and a fool.
lines.plainText: Marry here's grace and a codpiece that's a wise man and a fool

lines.text: Alas, sir, are you here? Things that love night
lines.plainText: Alas sir are you here Things that love night

lines.text: Love not such nights as these; the wrathful skies
lines.plainText: Love not such nights as these the wrathful skies

lines.text: Gallow the very wanderers of the dark,
lines.plainText: Gallow the very wanderers of the dark

lines.text: And make them keep their caves. Since I was man,
lines.plainText: And make them keep their caves Since I was man

lines.text: Such sheets of fire, such bursts of horrid thunder,
lines.plainText: Such sheets of fire such bursts of horrid thunder

lines.text: Such groans of roaring wind and rain I never
lines.plainText: Such groans of roaring wind and rain I never

lines.text: Remember to have heard. Man's nature cannot carry
lines.plainText: Remember to have heard Man's nature cannot carry

lines.text: Th'affliction, nor the fear.
lines.plainText: Th'affliction nor the fear

lines.text: Let the great gods,
lines.plainText: Let the great gods

lines.text: That keep this dreadful pudder o'er our heads,
lines.plainText: That keep this dreadful pudder o'er our heads

lines.text: Find out their enemies now. Tremble, thou wretch,
lines.plainText: Find out their enemies now Tremble thou wretch

lines.text: That hast within thee undivulged crimes
lines.plainText: That hast within thee undivulged crimes

lines.text: Unwhipp'd of justice. Hide thee, thou bloody hand;
lines.plainText: Unwhipp'd of justice Hide thee thou bloody hand

lines.text: Thou perjur'd, and thou simular of virtue
lines.plainText: Thou perjur'd and thou simular of virtue

lines.text: That art incestuous. Caitiff, to pieces shake
lines.plainText: That art incestuous Caitiff to pieces shake

lines.text: That under covert and convenient seeming
lines.plainText: That under covert and convenient seeming

lines.text: Hast practis'd on man's life: close pent-up guilts,
lines.plainText: Hast practis'd on man's life close pentup guilts

lines.text: Rive your concealing continents, and cry
lines.plainText: Rive your concealing continents and cry

lines.text: These dreadful summoners grace. I am a man
lines.plainText: These dreadful summoners grace I am a man

lines.text: More sinn'd against than sinning.
lines.plainText: More sinn'd against than sinning

lines.text: Alack, bareheaded!
lines.plainText: Alack bareheaded

lines.text: Gracious my lord, hard by here is a hovel;
lines.plainText: Gracious my lord hard by here is a hovel

lines.text: Some friendship will it lend you 'gainst the tempest:
lines.plainText: Some friendship will it lend you 'gainst the tempest

lines.text: Repose you there, whilst I to this hard house,—
lines.plainText: Repose you there whilst I to this hard house

lines.text: More harder than the stones whereof 'tis rais'd;
lines.plainText: More harder than the stones whereof 'tis rais'd

lines.text: Which even but now, demanding after you,
lines.plainText: Which even but now demanding after you

lines.text: Denied me to come in,—return, and force
lines.plainText: Denied me to come inreturn and force

lines.text: Their scanted courtesy.
lines.plainText: Their scanted courtesy

lines.text: My wits begin to turn.
lines.plainText: My wits begin to turn

lines.text: Come on, my boy. How dost, my boy? Art cold?
lines.plainText: Come on my boy How dost my boy Art cold

lines.text: I am cold myself. Where is this straw, my fellow?
lines.plainText: I am cold myself Where is this straw my fellow

lines.text: The art of our necessities is strange,
lines.plainText: The art of our necessities is strange

lines.text: That can make vile things precious. Come, your hovel.
lines.plainText: That can make vile things precious Come your hovel

lines.text: Poor fool and knave, I have one part in my heart
lines.plainText: Poor fool and knave I have one part in my heart

lines.text: That's sorry yet for thee.
lines.plainText: That's sorry yet for thee

lines.text: [Singing.]
lines.plainText: Singing

lines.text: He that has and a little tiny wit,
lines.plainText: He that has and a little tiny wit

lines.text: With heigh-ho, the wind and the rain,
lines.plainText: With heighho the wind and the rain

lines.text: Must make content with his fortunes fit,
lines.plainText: Must make content with his fortunes fit

lines.text: Though the rain it raineth every day.
lines.plainText: Though the rain it raineth every day

lines.text: True, boy. Come, bring us to this hovel.
lines.plainText: True boy Come bring us to this hovel

lines.text: This is a brave night to cool a courtezan. I'll speak a prophecy ere I go:
lines.plainText: This is a brave night to cool a courtezan I'll speak a prophecy ere I go

lines.text: When priests are more in word than matter;
lines.plainText: When priests are more in word than matter

lines.text: When brewers mar their malt with water;
lines.plainText: When brewers mar their malt with water

lines.text: When nobles are their tailors' tutors;
lines.plainText: When nobles are their tailors' tutors

lines.text: No heretics burn'd, but wenches' suitors;
lines.plainText: No heretics burn'd but wenches' suitors

lines.text: When every case in law is right;
lines.plainText: When every case in law is right

lines.text: No squire in debt, nor no poor knight;
lines.plainText: No squire in debt nor no poor knight

lines.text: When slanders do not live in tongues;
lines.plainText: When slanders do not live in tongues

lines.text: Nor cut-purses come not to throngs;
lines.plainText: Nor cutpurses come not to throngs

lines.text: When usurers tell their gold i' the field;
lines.plainText: When usurers tell their gold i' the field

lines.text: And bawds and whores do churches build,
lines.plainText: And bawds and whores do churches build

lines.text: Then shall the realm of Albion
lines.plainText: Then shall the realm of Albion

lines.text: Come to great confusion:
lines.plainText: Come to great confusion

lines.text: Then comes the time, who lives to see't,
lines.plainText: Then comes the time who lives to see't

lines.text: That going shall be us'd with feet.
lines.plainText: That going shall be us'd with feet

lines.text: This prophecy Merlin shall make; for I live before his time.
lines.plainText: This prophecy Merlin shall make for I live before his time
